listening1.context: You are going to hear a conversation between Huda and Hamad.

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: Hi Hamad! Mrs Aisha says that our school is going to start a blog. She asked me to help, and I'd like you to join the team.

script.speaker: Hamad
script.text: Of course! I love writing. What will the blog be about? Sports, maybe?

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: Sports is a good idea, but the team has chosen to write about school life, such as events, trips and student news.

script.speaker: Hamad
script.text: That sounds interesting. Who will be able to read the blog? Only students?

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: Students, parents and teachers. Everybody will be able to read it, but only the team will be allowed to write the posts.

script.speaker: Hamad
script.text: I see. How often will we publish a new post? Every day?

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: That's too much work. Every day is impossible, and every week is too slow. We'll publish a post every three days.

script.speaker: Hamad
script.text: All right. What about photographs? Can we put photos of students on the blog?

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: Only with their permission. This is a rule of the school, because their privacy is important. We'll never show a student's full name without permission.

script.speaker: Hamad
script.text: That's a very good rule. Which website shall we use to make the blog?

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: Mr Yahya, the computer teacher, suggested a free website. It's easy to use, and it has nice colours.

script.speaker: Hamad
script.text: Great. When will we meet to plan the first post?

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: On Monday, during the break, in the room of the computer teacher. Please bring your laptop.

script.speaker: Hamad
script.text: I will. What shall we write in the very first post?

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: I think we should introduce the team. Each of us can write two sentences about ourselves, and add a photo.

script.speaker: Hamad
script.text: That's a lovely idea. I can also write about the new library, because I visited it yesterday.

script.speaker: Huda
script.text: Wonderful. Let's write the plan down now.

items.q: What will the school blog be about?
Who will be allowed to write the posts?
How often will they publish a new post?
When can they put a student's photograph on the blog?
What will they write in the first post?

listening2.context: You are going to hear a talk about Mesopotamia.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Hello, everyone. Today I am going to tell you about Mesopotamia, the land between two rivers, and about its great gifts to the world.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Mesopotamia was in the area of modern Iraq. Its name comes from Greek words that mean the land between the rivers. The two rivers were the Tigris and the Euphrates. The rivers gave water to farmers, and the people grew wheat and barley in the fertile land.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: The first cities in the world grew here more than five thousand years ago. One of the earliest was Ur. Later, Babylon became the most famous city. Its king, Hammurabi, wrote a set of laws about three thousand seven hundred years ago, and the laws were carved on a tall stone for everybody to read.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: The people of Mesopotamia were also great inventors. Around the year thirty-five hundred before Christ, they invented the wheel. At first, they used it to make pots, and later they put wheels on carts, which helped farmers and traders to move heavy loads.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: They also invented one of the first systems of writing. It is called cuneiform. Writers pressed a sharp stick into soft clay to make wedge-shaped marks, and then they dried the clay in the sun. Thousands of these clay tablets still exist today. Some of them are lists of goods, and others are letters and stories.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: The Sumerians, who lived in Mesopotamia, also gave us the sixty-minute hour. They counted in sixty, and that is why we have sixty seconds in a minute and sixty minutes in an hour. They also built tall temples, called ziggurats, which looked like giant steps.

script.speaker: Presenter
script.text: Many of our everyday ideas come from this ancient land. Thank you for listening.

short.q: What are the names of the two rivers? Give one.
Which king wrote a famous set of laws?
What is the name of the writing system made on clay?
What were the tall temples called?

tf.statement: Mesopotamia was in the area of modern Iraq.
The wheel was first used to make pots.
Clay tablets were dried in a fire.
